subject: Fintecha: private inference network runbook & SLO confirmations
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Adrian Keller <adrian.keller@fintecha.io>, ops+network@fintecha.io
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fintecha: private inference network runbook & SLO confirmations

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the Fintecha network and infra team. Below is a short recap of the performance targets we discussed and the runbook we propose to validate capacity for your Private (VPC) deployment. I added Dylan and Rishi to own the test plans and VPN/peering details.

High-level SLOs you validated on the call:
- Latency: P50 goal <= 80 ms (in-region); P95 <= 200 ms for 2k token responses (streaming enabled).
- Throughput: sustained 2,000 tokens/sec aggregate for inference pipeline across 4 shards.
- Concurrency: support 500 concurrent streaming sessions with 20 TPS per session burst tolerance.
- Egress: baseline 600 Mbps available for model outputs; tolerate 20% headroom during spikes.

Key network constraints / environment notes from Fintecha:
- Primary region: us-east-1.
- VPN appliance: Juniper SRX with MTU 1500, IPSec tunnels to Redwood edge.
- Peer: direct VPC peering planned to redwood-prod-vpc (VPC peering, not transit).

Proposed validation runbook (next steps):
1) Redwood to run synthetic streaming and KV-cache-aware tests from our public test harness (link below).
2) Fintecha to provide a short-lived test user and pre-configured VPN endpoint + sample network map (we received vpn_network_map.pdf — thanks).
3) Joint run: 3 rounds — baseline latency sweep, concurrency ramp to 500 sessions, and egress saturation test.
4) Capture packet-level stats (latency, retransmits), per-hop RTT, and per-token latency breakdown.
5) If P95 > 200 ms, exercise fallbacks: (a) lower decoder chunk sizes; (b) route to local cache-enabled shard; (c) enable token-level batching knob.

Deliverables and owners:
- Redwood: test harness results, raw traces, and fintecha_slo_matrix.xlsx populated (Dylan).
- Fintecha: VPN endpoint credentials, firewall egress rules, and confirmation of peering window (Adrian).
- Timeline: aim to complete joint run within 4 business days after credentials exchange.

Attachments: fintecha_slo_matrix.xlsx (template), redwood_preflight-runbook.md (draft checklist), vpn_network_map.pdf (from Fintecha).

Test harness: https://redwood.nyc/test-harness/fintecha-net-run
Preflight checklist: https://drive.redwood.com/fintecha/preflight-checklist

Next steps (for this week):
- Adrian: share VPN test creds and an expected maintenance window for peering (reply to this thread).
- Dylan: will sketch the exact ramp schedule and attach to the SLO matrix.
- Rishi: will confirm expected model response sizes and KV cache behavior needed for the run.

Thanks — looking forward to the joint run.

—
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0128
https://www.redwood.com

From: Adrian Keller <adrian.keller@fintecha.io>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: ops+network@fintecha.io, procurement@fintecha.io
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 17:32:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fintecha: private inference network runbook & SLO confirmations

Thanks Tessa — Adrian here. Quick clarifications from our side after reviewing the runbook:
- We can allocate a 1-hour peering window on Tue (04/20) 10:00–11:00 EDT. That should be sufficient for the ramp tests; we can extend if needed.
- VPN details: we will create a test IPSec tunnel using the SRX; shared secret and public endpoint will be sent over our secure vault (expect creds today).
- Bandwidth: the egress path currently sustained ~700 Mbps to Redwood's edge during internal tests; we will reserve 600–800 Mbps for the run.
- MTU and TCP MSS issues: we have observed occasional PMTUD blackholes when the MTU is forced; please include a quick test for path MTU and MSS tuning in the runbook.
- Model size: production models return around 1.8k tokens per request on average when summarizing; worst-case bursts up to 3k tokens.

One ask from our infra lead: can Redwood include a short script (iperf-like) that runs inside our VPN and reports per-minute throughput and jitter? That would help us detect transient drops.

I'll push the VPN creds to your ops@redwood secure channel and notify here once available.

— Adrian
Adrian Keller
Head of Platform, Fintecha Inc.
adrian.keller@fintecha.io
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Adrian Keller <adrian.keller@fintecha.io>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fintecha: private inference network runbook & SLO confirmations

Appreciate the details, Adrian — that bandwidth headroom is helpful. Quick notes from Redwood test engineering and the exact ramp we propose:
- Phase A (baseline): 50 concurrent streams, 1k tokens/sec aggregate, 15 minute steady-state to capture per-hop RTTs and retransmits.
- Phase B (concurrency ramp): linear ramp to 500 concurrent streaming sessions over 20 minutes while maintaining average tokens/sec. Measure P50/P95 per 2-minute window.
- Phase C (egress saturation): incrementally push output bandwidth to 80% of the reserved egress (i.e., target ~560 Mbps) for 10 minutes to verify egress shaping and QoS.

Instrumentation we will collect (we'll deliver CSVs and pcap snippets):
- Per-token latency series (clientTx -> serverRx -> modelGen -> serverTx -> clientRx).
- Socket-level retransmit counts and instantaneous throughput.
- Application-level streaming chunk sizes and observed per-chunk latency.

Scripts we will provide:
- iperf-like Python harness to run inside your subnet (small agent, no root required).
- a short MTU probe to detect PMTUD issues and fallback to MSS clamp.

Requesting from Fintecha before Wed EOD:
1) VPN test credentials + endpoint (Adrian).
2) Confirmation of firewall outbound ports 443 and 5222 for our telemetry agent (if you prefer different ports call it out).
3) A short example request payload/expected token distribution (Rishi, this helps us tune chunking).

I'll attach the ramp schedule to the SLO matrix and mark owners.

— Dylan
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Adrian Keller <adrian.keller@fintecha.io>, ops+network@fintecha.io
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, procurement@fintecha.io
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fintecha: private inference network runbook & SLO confirmations

Thanks Adrian — and thanks team. Quick confirmation and final logistics:
- We received the VPN map and will watch for creds in the secure channel. Once received, Dylan will schedule the baseline run during your Tue 10:00–11:00 EDT peering window.
- If the MTU probe flags issues, we'll automatically apply MSS clamp steps and re-run the short baseline (this is in the redwood_preflight-runbook.md attachment).
- Deliverables after the run (within 24 hours): populated fintecha_slo_matrix.xlsx, raw pcap snippets, aggregated latency CSV, and a short runbook note with recommended network tweaks (if any).

Final ask for procurement: if the joint run exposes any unexpected changes to required ports or escalation items, we'll open a short SOW amendment and route for a quick approval. procurement@fintecha.io, please confirm your standard SLA for such amendments.

I'll follow up after the run with a concise result email and next steps for production cutover (including suggested fallbacks: local shard pinning and token-batching profiles).

Thanks — Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_preflight-runbook.md, fintecha_slo_matrix.xlsx
